body: Heavy lanes on the final head 2649bb17e: `kernel heavy`, `motion heavy` and `app heavy` ran 253 steps after one release build. 0 failed, 53.3 min. The known-fail steps of #1950 and #2849 are red as expected. The quick gate is green on this head, except #3119 (CRLF, not touched here). The PR body has the details. Ready for review.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 2649bb17ee8a7c1b5713bed64a1f077af2fc5b49 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** One test target does not compile on Linux and macOS. The PR body also has no screenshot of the new modal.

Review tier: SAFETY. The change sets the scale of imported STEP geometry.

### What looks good

- The kernel writes the stated unit into each representation context before the read. Thus the tolerance, the edge-gap cap and the chord are in the same unit as the geometry. The decision record explains why a mesh scale after the read is not correct.
- A file that states its own unit keeps it. The note says when the caller's unit is not used.
- A unit outside 0.001..=1000 mm is refused by name. A unit for an STL or OBJ file is refused before parsing.
- The prompt is view state only. The answer goes through the command queue, and the import that lands is one undoable command. Cancel and Escape import nothing.
- MCP `import_model` and `cam.import` take `units`. `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and `cam.d.ts` are regenerated.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in the new non-test code.
- Nothing re-meshes stored `step_source` text. Saved projects open as before.
- I also tried two branches that the PR tests do not cover, in a local scratch test (not pushed). Both read at the correct scale (area ratio 645.16 for inches):
  - a complex context with no `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT`;
  - a plain `GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT('…','3D',3)`.

### Results (locally, macOS arm64, trial merge with upstream/main `f036dddad`)

The trial merge is clean.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Build `camcraft-kernel`, `camcraft-geometry`, `camcraft-ui` tests | ok |
| Build `camcraft-app` tests | **FAILED**: `cadmpeg_import` (8 x E0061, see item 1) |
| Quick gate `--base upstream/main` (1039 steps; stopped by my 20 min limit after 973 step logs) | 972 ok, 1 red: `app suites: tool_gate` `the_refusal_names_a_fitting_catalog_entry`. Main is red on the same test (#3170, fix in #3172). It is not from this PR. |
| Steps that the stopped gate did not reach, run by hand | all ok (list below) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | **FAILED** on the PR as it is (item 1). Clean when item 1 is fixed locally. |

Run by hand, all green:

- kernel: `agreement`, `machining_mesh_bounds`, `machining_mesh_open`, `step_edge_gap`, `step_short_units`, `step_twisted_flank`, `step_import`, `step_assumed_unit` (3).
- app: `lib` (297), `step_units_import` (5), `import_step_outward`, `import_step_closed_shell`, `import_step_corner_blend`, `import_step_curve_guard`, `import_step_guard`, `import_step_guard_default_cap`, `import_step_open_shell`, `mcp_live`, `mcp_doc_drift`, `scripting`, `step_fidelity`, `step_nesting`, `keep_law`, `kept_parts_live`, `mcp_setup_mount_trace`, `stock_source_verdict`.
- app `cadmpeg_import`: 13 passed, but only after the local fix of item 1. The stub output states its unit, so the converted path imports as before.
- ui (from `crates/ui`): `lib` (1391 passed, 7 ignored), `egui_app`, `models`, `shell`, `fixtures`, `operations`, `feedback`.

**Extra suites run** (the PR changes the STEP import code):

- `cargo test -p camcraft-kernel --test step_agreement`: 26 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-kernel --test machining_mesh`: 7 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test feature_edge_g1_join`: 5 passed.
- No file under `testdata/` changed.

**Heavy lanes:** I did not run them. The author reports `kernel heavy`, `motion heavy` and `app heavy` on the final head: 253 steps ok, 0 failed (Windows x86_64).

### Mutations (each reverted after the run)

1. `crates/geometry/src/step.rs`: the `MissingUnits` refusal is removed. **Red**: `step_units_import` `a_step_file_with_no_length_unit_is_refused_by_name_without_a_unit` and `mcp_import_model_takes_the_unit_and_refuses_without_it`.
2. `crates/kernel/src/step_assumed_unit.rs`: the conversion factor is always `1.0`. **Red**: kernel `a_unitless_file_reads_in_the_unit_that_the_caller_states`, and app `a_unit_stated_at_import_reads_the_unitless_file_in_it_and_says_so`.
3. `crates/ui/src/state.rs`: the `StepUnitsMissing` arm of `finish_import` is disabled. **Red**: 3 of the 4 `step_units_tests`.

No golden file changes in this PR.

### Requested before merge

1. **`crates/app/tests/cadmpeg_import.rs:118`** (also lines 127, 147, 156, 171, 178, 183 and 273): these calls of `cadmpeg::load_open_within` still give 3 arguments. The PR adds a fourth argument, `units`. The calls are in the `#[cfg(unix)]` module (line 46), so the Windows quick gate did not compile them. On Linux and macOS the test target does not build, and `clippy --all-targets` fails. The post-merge gate runs on Linux, so main goes red. Fix: add `, None` as the fourth argument at each call. Then run the `cadmpeg_import` suite and clippy on Linux or macOS, or ask a reviewer to do it.
2. **Screenshots of the UI change.** The PR adds the **Length unit** modal (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/step_units_prompt.rs`). The body says "No screenshot of the new modal yet". Add a before and after screenshot to the PR body. Put the images on your fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch and link them. Do not commit the images to this branch.

### Notes (not blocking)

- These files were already over 400 lines and grow: `crates/ui/src/state.rs` (+27), `crates/app/src/script/api.rs` (+6), `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` (+2).
- This is a `feat` PR. It merges at the next minor cut.
- NeoTech set `needs-maintainer` on this PR. I keep that label and add `needs-rework`.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Back to draft for the review fixes: the four-argument `cadmpeg::load_open_within` calls in `crates/app/tests/cadmpeg_import.rs` (the `#[cfg(unix)]` module), and the stale `step_units_next` unit. Then the gates run again and the PR is flagged ready again.

Review fixes on b5637db2b. Thank you for the two reviews.

mkinney, requested items:

1. `crates/app/tests/cadmpeg_import.rs`: each of the eight `cadmpeg::load_open_within` calls (lines 118, 127, 147, 156, 171, 178, 183, 273) now passes `None` as the fourth argument. The module is `#[cfg(unix)]`, so my Windows gates do not compile it. Please build `cadmpeg_import` and clippy on Linux or macOS in the re-review.
2. Screenshot: the PR body has the Length unit prompt in the section "Screenshot" since 15:20 UTC. AGENTS.md has no `pr-screenshots` branch rule, so the image is a GitHub upload. There is no "before" image: before this PR, the import read the file as millimetres and showed no prompt.

NeoTech, notes:

- `step_units_next`: fixed. Each import start now takes the chosen unit, whatever its file. Pinned by `step_units_tests::a_chosen_unit_never_waits_for_a_later_import_of_the_same_file`.
- Linked-file re-import: `troubleshooting.md` now says that the next import, a re-import included, asks again.
- `length unit: mm, mm`: this cannot occur. `step_length_units::read` keeps each distinct unit one time (it compares the bits of the value), and the stated unit is the same value in each context. Thus a unitless file with many contexts gives one name.

Gates on b5637db2b (Windows x86_64): quick gate 1032 of 1033 steps ok, and the red step is #3119 (CRLF). Heavy lanes `kernel`, `motion` and `app`: 253 steps ok, 0 failed. Clippy on app and ui is clean. The PR body has the details.

Ready for a re-review.

**Code is clean on macOS. The PR does not merge with the current `main`: merge `main` into the branch.**

Review tier: SAFETY. The change sets the scale of imported STEP geometry. NeoTech's review of this head asked for a Linux or macOS build. This review builds and tests that.

## My earlier change request (head `2649bb17e`)

Both items are done on this head. I withdraw that change request.

1. `crates/app/tests/cadmpeg_import.rs` (`#[cfg(unix)]` module): compiles and passes on macOS. 13 passed, 0 failed.
2. Screenshot of the Length unit modal: it is in the PR body.

## Conflicts with `main` (`6e641dac7`)

A trial merge stops on three files. Each conflict is a line that both sides added or changed:

- `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs`: keep this PR's `import_model` row. Keep the `get_job` row from `main` (`summary`, `super::compact::s_get_job`).
- `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`: the same two rows. Generate the file again after the merge.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs`: keep the two window calls, `step_units_prompt::window` and `dxf_units_dialog::window` (#1863).

For this review only, I resolved the conflicts as above in a local trial merge. I did not push it. All the results below are on that trial merge.

## Results (macOS arm64, local trial merge of `b5637db2b` with `upstream/main` `6e641dac7`)

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 1104 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 20.9 min. This includes clippy `-D warnings`, `step_units_import`, `import_step_outward`, `import_step_closed_shell`, `example_catalog` (3 suites), the ui lib and `ai_guide_calls_match_live_tools_list`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test cadmpeg_import`: 13 passed.

### Extra suites run

- `cargo test -p camcraft-kernel --test step_agreement`: 29 passed.
- kernel `machining_mesh` (and `_bounds`, `_open`, `_parity`, `_redivide`, `_shortfalls`): ok, in the quick gate.
- `camcraft-app --test feature_edge_g1_join`: ok, in the quick gate.
- Each of the 34 STEP files in `testdata/models/` states a length unit. No fixture becomes a refusal.

### Mutations (each restored after the run)

- M1: `solidcore_step.rs` does not call `step_assumed_unit::assume`. Result: RED. `step_assumed_unit` has 2 of 3 tests red (`a_unitless_file_reads_in_the_unit_that_the_caller_states`, `a_stated_unit_out_of_range_is_refused_by_name`).
- M2: `geometry/src/step.rs` does not refuse a file with no length unit. Result: RED. `step_units_import` has 2 of 5 tests red (`a_step_file_with_no_length_unit_is_refused_by_name_without_a_unit`, `mcp_import_model_takes_the_unit_and_refuses_without_it`).

### Heavy lanes

- The diff reaches `kernel heavy`, `motion heavy` and `app heavy`. The body reports 253 steps ok on this head. That run used an older `main`.
- This review did not run them: not run - owed. The merge of `main` makes a new head. The heavy lanes must run again on that head.

## What looks good

- A file with no length unit is refused by name (`ImportError::StepUnitsMissing`). It is not read as millimetres. A unit from the caller is written into the representation contexts before the read. Thus the tolerance, the edge-gap cap and the chord use the same unit as the geometry.
- A file that states its own unit keeps it. The note names a caller unit that the reader did not use.
- An open of a saved project does not read the STEP source again. Saved projects do not change.
- Holders, fixtures and tool bodies use `load_model_graded`. They refuse a file with no length unit by name. They do not guess.
- The answer goes through the command queue (`ResolveStepUnits`). The import that lands is one undoable command.
- No posted program, golden or snapshot PNG changed. No `Cargo.toml`, `build.rs`, `scripts/` or `.github/` change. No process file changed.
- The new files are below 400 lines and have provenance lines. The body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #1874`, and the decision record is `docs/decisions/1874-step-length-units.md`.

## Notes (not blocking)

- `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs`, `crates/app/src/script/api.rs` and `crates/ui/src/state.rs` were already longer than 400 lines. They grow by a small number of lines. The body says this.
- `main` now has a DXF units prompt (#1863). The two prompts have different titles and wording. A later polish issue can make them the same.

## Label

- `conflicts` stays. Merge `main` into the branch (no rebase, no force-push), resolve as above, and gate again.
- I remove `needs-rework`. My change request is met, and this review found no defect in the code.
- No `merge-ready`. The PR does not merge with `main`, and the heavy lanes are owed on the new head.

A maintainer approves and merges this PR by hand.
